name: Shri Kedar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple on Madanachala hill at Hajo, completed in 1753 under the Ahom king Rajeswara Singha; it is one of the principal shrines of the Hajo pilgrimage cluster in lower Assam.
story: The linga in the central chamber is revered as swayambhu, said to have arisen of itself rather than being carved.

name: Pathrol Kali Temple
significance: A Kali shrine near Madhupur in the Santhal Pargana, attributed to Raja Digvijay Singh some six or seven centuries ago; it draws large crowds at Kali Puja and during the Durga festival.

name: Buddha Samyak Darshan Museum and Memorial Stupa
significance: A modern memorial stupa and museum at Vaishali built to enshrine the relics of the Buddha that had been given to the Licchavi rulers of the city, approved in 2013 and completed for inauguration in July 2025. It was assembled from more than 42,000 Rajasthani sandstone blocks without modern reinforcement.
story: Tradition holds that after the Buddha's mahaparinirvana his remains were divided into eight shares among eight kings, each of whom raised a stupa over his portion.

name: Nidhivan
significance: A dense sacred grove of tulsi and other trees in the heart of Vrindavan, containing the Rang Mahal, the Bansichori Radharani shrine and the Raslila Sthali, and associated with the saint-musician Swami Haridas.
story: Devotees believe Radha and Krishna still dance the rasa-lila in the grove at night, so it is barricaded shut after dark.

name: Khema Baba Temple
significance: A folk shrine at Baytu in the Barmer desert dedicated to Khema Baba, a social reformer of Baytu Bhopji who came to be venerated as a deity across western Rajasthan and Gujarat.

name: Ahmedabad Kali Bari
significance: A Kali temple in west Ahmedabad built in 2014 by the Bengal Cultural Association of Ahmedabad; it serves the city's Bengali community and also houses shrines to Shiva, Rama, Sita, Hanuman and Krishna.

name: Arulmigu Munthi Vinayagar Temple
significance: A Ganesha temple in the Puliakulam quarter of Coimbatore, opened in its present form in 1982, known for a monolithic granite Vinayagar image about 19 feet high and weighing some 190 tonnes.

name: Tiruvirkudi Veerataneswarar Temple
significance: A Shiva temple in the Kaveri delta whose present masonry structure was raised by the Cholas in the 9th century and enlarged by the Thanjavur Nayaks; it is one of the ashta-virattanam shrines marking Shiva's heroic deeds.
story: Shiva is said to have destroyed the demon Jalandhara here, after Vishnu had undone the chastity of Jalandhara's wife Tulasi that made him invincible.

name: Changdeva Temple
significance: A stone temple at the Tapi-Purna confluence dedicated to the yogi Changdeva Maharaj, built in dove-tailed black rock in the Hemadpanthi manner; ASI excavations from 2008 uncovered foundations of earlier stone temples and images of Ganesha, Vishnu and Hanuman.
story: Local legend holds that the temple was raised in the course of a single night that lasted six months.

name: Mamal Temple (Mamaleshwar)
builtDisplay: c. 400 CE, rebuilt in the medieval period
significance: One of the oldest surviving Shiva temples in Kashmir, dated to about 400 CE and rebuilt in medieval times; the Rajatarangini records King Jayasimha crowning it with a golden kalasa.
story: The name is glossed as 'Mam Mal', 'do not go', from the tale that Parvati set Ganesha to guard the spot and Shiva, refused entry, struck off his head and replaced it with an elephant's.

name: Jagannath Temple, Dibrugarh
significance: An 85-foot Jagannath temple in Dibrugarh completed in 2014 at the initiative of Janaki Ballabh Patnaik, then Governor of Assam, and run by the Sri Sri Jagannath Cultural Trust; its plan follows an earlier form of the Puri temple and its grounds hold seven subsidiary shrines.

name: Agatheeswarar Temple, Karur
significance: A Shiva temple at the river confluence near Karur, over a thousand years old and credited to Rajendra Chola I (r. 1014-1044).
story: The sage Agastya is said to have consecrated a lingam of sand here before Vaali could install a lingam brought from Kashi, so Vaali founded the Valeeswarar temple on the opposite bank instead.

name: Maha Mrityunjay Temple
significance: A Shiva temple near Puranigudam in Nagaon district begun in 2003 by Acharya Bhrigu Giri Maharaj and finished in February 2021; the 126-foot structure is itself shaped as a shivalinga and is claimed to be the largest of its kind.
story: The site is held to be where the guru Shukracharya recited the Mahamrityunjaya mantra.

name: Haleshwar Sthan
significance: A Shiva shrine north-west of Sitamarhi town in the Mithila region, documented as older than the 17th century and one of the busier pilgrimage sites of northern Bihar, especially during Shravan.
story: The temple is said to have been founded by King Videha while he performed the putra-yeshti sacrifice, and named Haleshwarnath after him.

name: Chaukhandi Stupa
significance: A terraced brick stupa at Sarnath marking the place where the Buddha is said to have met his first disciples on the way from Bodh Gaya; an octagonal tower was later raised on it by Govardhan, son of Raja Todar Mal, to mark a visit by the Mughal emperor Humayun.

name: Kshemkari Mata Temple
significance: A goddess temple at the old town of Bhinmal in Jalore district dedicated to Kshemkari Devi, locally called Khimaj Mata.

name: Badhangarhi Temple
significance: A hilltop Kali temple in the Pindar valley of Garhwal, founded by a Katyuri king and altered in 1670 and again in the colonial period, when Commissioner G. W. Traill built a shrine for a relocated Nanda Devi image.
story: Local tradition says Traill was struck with snow-blindness by the offended goddess and recovered only after building her a temple.

name: Baba Mukteshwar Dham
significance: A Shiva temple at Deohar in Madhubani district, believed to be roughly two hundred years old and built in the Tirhut idiom of Mithila; excavation at the site brought up a shivalinga and images of Ganesha and Parvati that were installed for worship.

name: Shri Chamunda Devi Mandir
significance: A Shakta temple on the Baner river in Kangra district, roughly four centuries old, which houses an image brought down from the far older hill shrine of Aadi Himani Chamunda.
story: A king and his priest are said to have prayed for the goddess's leave to move her image to an accessible spot, and she revealed its location to the priest in a dream.
